final_proof:
Write the multiindices as \(\alpha=(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_n)\) and \(\beta=(\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_n)\). Recall that a multiindex has nonnegative integer components. For a tuple \(z=(z_1,\ldots,z_n)\) and a multiindex \(\gamma\), set \(z^\gamma=\prod_{j=1}^n z_j^{\gamma_j}\), where, as usual, \(z_j^0=1\) for every real \(z_j\). The inequalities \(0\leq\beta\leq\alpha\) mean \(0\leq\beta_j\leq\alpha_j\) for every \(j\), and the multiindex binomial coefficient is
\[
\binom{\alpha}{\beta}=\prod_{j=1}^n\binom{\alpha_j}{\beta_j}.
\]
Since addition of tuples is componentwise, the definition of a multiindex power and the ordinary binomial theorem give
\[
\begin{aligned}
(x+y)^\alpha
&=\prod_{j=1}^n(x_j+y_j)^{\alpha_j}\\
&=\prod_{j=1}^n\left(\sum_{k_j=0}^{\alpha_j}\binom{\alpha_j}{k_j}x_j^{k_j}y_j^{\alpha_j-k_j}\right).
\end{aligned}
\]
All these sums are finite, so repeated use of the distributive law expands the product as
\[
\sum_{k_1=0}^{\alpha_1}\cdots\sum_{k_n=0}^{\alpha_n}
\left(\prod_{j=1}^n\binom{\alpha_j}{k_j}\right)
\left(\prod_{j=1}^n x_j^{k_j}\right)
\left(\prod_{j=1}^n y_j^{\alpha_j-k_j}\right).
\]
The tuples \(\beta=(k_1,\ldots,k_n)\) occurring in this iterated sum are exactly the multiindices satisfying \(0\leq\beta\leq\alpha\), each occurring once. For such a \(\beta\), the three products in the summand are respectively \(\binom{\alpha}{\beta}\), \(x^\beta\), and \(y^{\alpha-\beta}\). Consequently,
\[
(x+y)^\alpha=\sum_{0\leq\beta\leq\alpha}\binom{\alpha}{\beta}x^\beta y^{\alpha-\beta},
\]
as claimed.
